# mdok

> mdok turns ordinary Markdown into executable API workflow tests: keep copied curl syntax, add standard JMESPath checks and captures, and run the same reviewable source locally, in CI, or through MCP.

## Overview

mdok is a local, CLI-first tool for API workflow tests. The distributed binary (Homebrew and GitHub releases, 0.2.0+) is the Go implementation; the Rust workspace in the repository is the full-feature reference (MCP server, record/replay, Postman import, plan/list). An `.md` or `.mdok.md` document can contain TOML variables, `curl mdok` request fences, `jmespath mdok check` assertions, and `jmespath mdok capture` fences. The document remains API documentation while also becoming an executable test and an agent-readable repair target.

mdok does not replace curl with a new HTTP DSL. Request values are parsed as data inside one argv element, never reparsed as shell source. Planning happens before a request is sent. HTTP/HTTPS and loopback-safe local testing are the default execution surface. Policy controls hosts, schemes, files, redirects, body sizes, commands, and secrets; unsupported behavior is reported instead of silently ignored.

The CLI emits human, JSON, JSON Lines, and JUnit reports. A bare `mdok file.md` is an alias for `mdok test file.md`.

## Quickstart

Build and validate the canonical authentication example:

```sh
cargo build --release
cargo run -p mdok-cli -- lint mdok-prd/examples/auth-flow.md
cargo run -p mdok-cli -- plan mdok-prd/examples/auth-flow.md --var base_url=http://127.0.0.1:9800
cargo run -p mdok-cli -- test mdok-prd/examples/auth-flow.md --var base_url=http://127.0.0.1:9800
```

A deterministic local fixture can be started with `mdok-test-server --listen 127.0.0.1:0 --json-ready`.

The canonical workflow syntax is:

````markdown
# Authentication flow

```toml mdok vars
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:9800"
email = "agent@example.com"
password = "test-password"
```

```curl mdok name=login
curl --request POST "{{base_url}}/auth/login" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-raw '{"email":{{email|json}},"password":{{password|json}}}'
```

```jmespath mdok check=login
status == `200`
body.user.email == variables.email
type(body.access_token) == 'string'
```

```jmespath mdok capture=login
{access_token: body.access_token, user_id: body.user.id}
```

```curl mdok name=get_profile
curl "{{base_url}}/users/{{user_id|url}}" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer {{access_token|header}}"
```

```jmespath mdok check=get_profile
status == `200`
body.id == variables.user_id
```
````

## MCP

`mdok mcp serve` exposes a stdio Model Context Protocol server. MCP is the preferred interface for coding agents that need discoverable, policy-aware API workflow tools while keeping Markdown as the durable source and JSON as evidence.

The server advertises these seven tools through `tools/list`:

- `mdok_test`: execute a workflow and return the normal redacted JSON report.
- `mdok_lint`: validate Markdown without network execution.
- `mdok_plan`: return the normalized, redacted execution plan.
- `mdok_list`: inventory requests, checks, captures, and dependencies.
- `mdok_probe`: run bounded Postman-compatible JavaScript in the QuickJS sandbox.
- `mdok_import_postman`: generate Markdown and a review manifest from Postman Collection v2.1 JSON.
- `mdok_version`: report MDOK, curl compatibility, TLS, and QuickJS profile versions.

Recommended order: import a collection when needed, store and review the generated Markdown, call `mdok_lint`, call `mdok_plan`, then call `mdok_test`. Treat `requires_review` and manifest diagnostics as a stop condition. Network access defaults to offline in the probe path and remains subject to project policy.

Start the server after building:

```sh
cargo build --release -p mdok-cli
./target/release/mdok mcp serve
```

## Repo facts

- Rust workspace with a `mdok` CLI binary; C integrates the pinned curl parser/libcurl boundary.
- MIT licensed (`../LICENSE`).
- The release CLI is distributed as a single static binary; the website itself has no build step or external assets.
- Postman Collection v2.1 import is a review-first, one-way canonicalization into Markdown plus a provenance/diagnostic manifest.
- The QuickJS sandbox provides a bounded Postman-compatible JavaScript probe surface; unsupported APIs fail with named diagnostics.
- The repository includes a 495-fixture Markdown corpus and deterministic local HTTP fixture server.
